definitions.explanation: The act of dedicating or offering something to a deity, sacred purpose, or higher cause.

examples.japanese: {神|かみ}に{酒|さけ}を{奉献|ほうけん}する。
examples.english: We offer sake to the gods.

examples.japanese: この{建物|たてもの}は{平和|へいわ}のために{奉献|ほうけん}された。
examples.english: This building was dedicated to peace.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{初|はじ}めに{奉献|ほうけん}の{儀式|ぎしき}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: A dedication ceremony was held at the beginning of the festival.

notes:
{奉献|ほうけん} combines {奉|ほう} (to offer respectfully) and {献|けん} (to present, to dedicate). It is a formal word used in religious, ceremonial, or solemn contexts. In Shinto, it refers to making offerings to {神|かみ}; in Christianity, it refers to consecration or dedication.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {奉献|ほうけん}{式|しき} — dedication ceremony
- {奉献|ほうけん}{物|もの}/{奉献|ほうけん}{品|ひん} — offering; dedicated item
- {奉献|ほうけん}の{祈|いの}り — prayer of dedication

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {奉納|ほうのう} — offering to a shrine or temple (more commonly used in Shinto contexts)
- {献上|けんじょう} — presenting to a person of high rank
- {捧|ささ}げる — to offer; to devote (a more general verb)
